addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

3	description: "Mini-ERP feature gap analysis against the \"Koenang Resto\" reference HTML the user shared, and what's been built so far"
4	metadata:

8	---
9	
10	User wants KasirKu to grow toward a "mini ERP" (2026-07-08), modeled loosely on a reference prototype (`Koenang Resto` — a separate accounting + cost-control app, file at `D:\Users\ASTRI\Downloads\index.html`, an iframe shell only — actual module content in `modules/akuntansi.html`/`modules/costcontrol.html` was never shared). Explicit instruction: doesn't need to be complete, and must not disrupt the existing system — see [[project-purpose-saas-product]].
11	
12	**Why:** the reference's sidebar reveals the target feature set even without the module internals: Akuntansi (COA/Jurnal/Neraca/Arus Kas/Target vs Aktual), Cost Control & HPP (kalkulator HPP, database bahan, cost control, laporan COGS, tren harga), Operasional (pembelian, stok, penjualan, invoice, kas harian, rekon rekening, supplier/hutang), SDM (absensi, payroll, lembur, THR, karyawan).
13	
14	**Gap analysis against KasirKu's actual code (verified by reading source, not assumed):**
15	- Already covered, no rebuild needed: Laba Rugi (cash-basis, `reports/laba-rugi`), Payroll+Absensi, Kelola Produk/Bahan Baku, Riwayat Transaksi, Kelola Kasir.
16	- **Hitung HPP** — already exists: `products/[productId]/recipe/actions.ts` → `recalculateProductCost()` auto-recomputes `products.cost` from `product_recipes × ingredients.unit_cost` on every add/remove.
17	- **Cost Control (teori vs aktual)** — already exists in full inside `finance/page.tsx` (~line 187-256): COGS Teori (recipe-based) vs COGS Aktual (opening + pembelian − closing inventory), with a variance box and qualitative waste/efficiency notes. Not obvious from the nav alone — read the file before assuming this is missing.
18	- **Laporan COGS (per-produk/kategori breakdown)** — was genuinely missing; **built 2026-07-08** at `reports/cogs/page.tsx`, linked from the sidebar ("📐 Laporan COGS" in dashboard-shell.tsx) and cross-linked from `finance/page.tsx`'s Kontrol HPP section. Shows revenue/COGS/margin per category and per product, flags products with no HPP data (cost=0) and products under 20% margin.
19	- **Tren Harga bahan baku** — still missing, needs a new price-history table (`ingredients.unit_cost` only stores the current value, no history). Not started.
20	- Full double-entry **Akuntansi module** (COA, Jurnal, Neraca, Arus Kas, Target vs Aktual) — still entirely missing, and is a much bigger lift (new schema for accounts + journal lines, plus a decision on how it relates to the existing cash-basis Laba Rugi/Keuangan pages — replace or coexist?). Not started; user chose to do Cost Control/HPP first, accounting module "menyusul" (comes after).
21	- **Operasional gaps** not yet addressed: formal Pembelian (purchasing) records beyond the existing `expenses` category tagging, Supplier & Hutang (accounts payable) tracking — no supplier table exists yet.
22	
23	**How to apply:** before building anything else from this reference, grep/read the relevant existing page first — this module has repeatedly turned out to already cover more than the sidebar-only feature list suggested. As of 2026-07-09 every item originally identified in this gap analysis has been built and verified E2E — no queued next candidate remains; ask the user what's next if resuming this thread.
24	
25	**Formula audit — 2026-07-09**, after all the above was built, ran 4 parallel Explore agents auditing every calculation in the app (POS checkout/merchant-fee, HPP/COGS/weighted-avg cost, accounting/journal/balance-sheet, payroll/shift-close/ticket-pricing). Most formulas checked out clean (checkout math, weighted-average cost, Neraca arithmetic, Anggaran variance, payroll, shift-close, ticket pricing — the last one has existing passing unit tests, 38/38). **4 real bugs found, 1 fixed so far:**
26	1. **FIXED (commit bdbe337)**: Arus Kas (`accounting/arus-kas/page.tsx`) bucketed cash flow by `journal_entries.source`, but `public.post_journal_entry` (used by every purchase and expense posting, not just true manual entries) always writes `source='manual'` — so nearly all purchases/expenses were misclassified into "Investasi & Pendanaan" instead of "Operasional". Fixed by classifying by the counterparty account's type/code instead (modal→Pendanaan, Peralatan 1-500→Investasi, else→Operasional). Verified in browser: Beban Lain-lain, Bayar Utang Dagang, and a cash Persediaan purchase all correctly moved to "Aktivitas Operasional".
27	2. **FIXED (commit b928d51)**: `recalculateProductCost()` (`products/[productId]/recipe/actions.ts`) only used to re-fire on recipe line add/remove — never when an ingredient's `unit_cost` changed via `ingredients/actions.ts` `editIngredient`, `finance/actions.ts` `addExpense`, or `purchases/actions.ts` `addPurchase`, so `products.cost` (and downstream, `transaction_items.cost` snapshotted at sale time → COGS Teori) silently went stale. Fixed by extracting the calc into `src/lib/recalculate-product-cost.ts` (`recalculateProductCost` + a new `recalculateProductCostsForIngredient` that finds every product referencing a given ingredient and recalcs each) and calling the ingredient-scoped version from all three write sites whenever `unit_cost` actually changes. Verified in browser on "Toko Test Laporan": added Gula Pasir (50gr) to Roti Bakar's recipe (HPP → Rp1.350 at Rp27/gr), then edited Gula Pasir's price to Rp100/gr manually — Roti Bakar's HPP updated to Rp5.000 without touching the recipe. Then bought 100gr more via the Pembelian page (weighted avg → Rp106/gr) — HPP updated again to Rp5.300, confirming all three trigger paths work.
28	3. **FIXED (commit e02e62d, migration `20260709120000_fix_zero_total_hpp_posting.sql`)**: `checkout_transaction` only posted a journal entry `if v_total > 0`, but stock/ingredient consumption happens unconditionally — a 100%-discounted sale reduced inventory with no HPP/Persediaan journal line at all. Fixed by decoupling the Kas & Bank/Pendapatan lines (posted only when `v_total > 0`) from the HPP/Persediaan lines (posted independently whenever `v_total_cost > 0`), building `v_journal_lines` incrementally and only calling `private.post_journal` if at least 2 lines ended up in it. Mirrored the identical fix in `void_transaction`'s reversing entry. Verified end-to-end in browser on "Toko Test Laporan": sold 1 Roti Bakar (HPP Rp5.300) with a 100% order discount (INV-20260709-0001, total Rp0) — jurnal correctly posted a 2-line entry (debit 5-001 HPP / credit 1-200 Persediaan, Rp5.300, no Kas & Bank/Pendapatan lines). Then voided it with manager PIN — reversing entry correctly posted debit 1-200 / credit 5-001, Rp5.300. Neraca stayed balanced throughout.
29	4. **FIXED (commit 23c83ca)**: `purchases/actions.ts` and `finance/actions.ts` called the `post_journal_entry` RPC via `supabase.rpc(...)` without checking `{ error }`. Now `postExpenseJournal`/`postPurchaseJournal` return the error message (or null) instead of swallowing it, and both call sites plus the utang-payment RPC call in `addPurchasePayment` check it: on failure they log a `"warning"` activity entry (instead of the usual success level) with the error text, and return a form error telling the user the record saved but a manual correcting journal entry is needed at Akuntansi → Jurnal. Verified no regression on the happy path (a normal "Lain-lain" expense still saved silently with no error banner). The failure path itself wasn't exercised (would need deliberately breaking an account code) but the logic is a straightforward null-check/ternary, low risk.
30	
31	**All 4 formula-audit bugs are now fixed** (commits bdbe337, b928d51, e02e62d, 23c83ca) — not yet pushed to origin as of the last fix. See [[supabase-migrations-manual]] if any future fix here needs a new migration.
32	
33	**Supplier & Hutang (formal Pembelian) — built and verified E2E 2026-07-09**: migration `20260709110000_suppliers_purchases.sql` (see [[supabase-migrations-manual]]) adds `public.suppliers` (name/phone/address/notes, soft-delete), `public.purchases` (supplier_id nullable, category constrained to `'Bahan Baku'|'Barang Dagang'`, optional ingredient_id/product_id + qty, amount, paid_amount with a `paid_amount <= amount` check), and `public.purchase_payments` (installment log). Deliberately additive/separate from the existing `finance/actions.ts` `addExpense` "Pembelian Bahan Baku/Barang Dagang" categories — this is a new, more structured flow for supplier-attributed purchases that can be paid partially or fully on credit, not a replacement.
34	- New pages: `suppliers/page.tsx` (CRUD list + outstanding-utang badge computed from purchases) and `purchases/page.tsx` (record a purchase — mirrors `add-expense-form.tsx`'s ingredient/product conditional UI and weighted-average cost recalc exactly, plus a 3-way payment-mode picker: Lunas Sekarang / Bayar Sebagian / Semua Utang — with inline "+ Bayar" installment forms per unpaid purchase row).
35	- `purchases/actions.ts` `addPurchase` posts a journal entry via the same `post_journal_entry` RPC pattern as `finance/actions.ts` (debit 1-200 Persediaan for the full amount; credit 1-001 Kas & Bank for whatever's paid now, credit 2-001 Utang Dagang for the remainder — 2 or 3 lines depending on payment mode). `addPurchasePayment` posts debit 2-001 / credit 1-001 for each installment and rejects overpayment past the remaining balance. Ingredient purchases also insert into `ingredient_price_history` (source `'pembelian'`) same as the expense flow, see [[mini-erp-scope]]'s Tren Harga section above.
36	- Nav: "🧾 Pembelian & Hutang" and "🏬 Supplier" added to the Operasional sidebar group (not fnb-gated — retail businesses get both too, just without the ingredient option; tiket excluded like the rest of Operasional's inventory items).
37	- Verified in browser: added supplier "CV Sumber Rejeki", bought 500gr Gula Pasir for Rp15.000 fully on credit → journal posted debit Persediaan/credit Utang Dagang Rp15.000 correctly (2-line entry, no Kas & Bank line since paid_amount=0), stock updated 1000→1500gr. Paid Rp10.000 installment → journal posted debit Utang Dagang/credit Kas & Bank Rp10.000, purchase row updated to "Sisa Rp5.000", supplier badge showed "Utang Rp5.000", Neraca stayed balanced throughout (Aset = Kewajiban + Modal confirmed after each step).
38	- UI quirk hit during testing, useful for future preview-tool sessions on this project: clicking a `useActionState`-wired submit button (`<form action={formAction}>`, a React-specific mechanism) immediately after `window.location.href` navigation can silently no-op if it fires before hydration completes — no network request, no error, just nothing happens. Re-clicking (or waiting a beat) after confirming the click actually landed fixes it. This is distinct from the earlier-documented plain-`onClick`-button pattern (edit-ingredient-form.tsx-style inline forms), which doesn't have this hydration race since... actually both need hydration; the symptom just presents differently (edit forms fail to open at all if unhydrated, vs. server-action forms open fine but silently eat the submit).
39	
40	**Tren Harga bahan baku — built and verified E2E 2026-07-09**: new `public.ingredient_price_history` table (migration `20260709100000_ingredient_price_history.sql`, see [[supabase-migrations-manual]]) is an append-only log (`business_id`, `ingredient_id`, `unit_cost`, `source` in `awal`/`pembelian`/`manual`, `created_at`), backfilled with each existing ingredient's current price as an `awal` row. Two write sites: `finance/actions.ts` `addExpense` inserts a `pembelian` row when a "Pembelian Bahan Baku" expense changes the weighted-average `unit_cost`; `ingredients/actions.ts` `editIngredient` inserts a `manual` row when the manual-edit form changes `unit_cost` (compares against the pre-update value fetched first). New page `reports/price-trend/page.tsx` — period filter (30/90 hari/semua), naik/turun-harga summary counts, and a `<details>`-per-ingredient list (server-component-friendly, no client JS) showing current vs baseline price and full history on expand. Nav link "🏷️ Tren Harga" added next to "Bahan Baku" in the Operasional sidebar group (fnb-only, same gate as Bahan Baku itself). Verified in browser: bought Gula Pasir at a higher price → showed up as `pembelian` entry and flagged "Naik Harga: 1 bahan"; edited its price manually via the ingredients page's inline edit (a client-state form with no `<form>` tag — Simpan is a plain button, so driving it via preview tools requires the native-setter + dispatchEvent('input') trick, not `preview_fill`, to get React's onChange to fire) → showed up as a third `manual` entry, history list correctly ordered newest-first (Edit manual Rp25 → Pembelian Rp21 → Awal Rp18).
41	
42	**Akuntansi module — built 2026-07-08** (user explicitly chose auto-posting from transactions, and all 4 reports at once, overriding the "doesn't need to be complete" framing for this specific piece):
43	- Schema: `public.accounts` (Chart of Accounts, seeded per-business via trigger + backfill with a standard Indonesian F&B/retail COA — Kas & Bank, Persediaan, Utang Dagang, Modal Pemilik, Pendapatan Penjualan, Beban Pokok Penjualan, Beban Gaji/Sewa/Listrik/Marketing/Perlengkapan/Lain-lain), `public.journal_entries` + `public.journal_lines` (double-entry, journal tables are SELECT-only from the client — all writes go through `private.post_journal()` so an unbalanced entry can never be persisted), `public.budgets` (Target vs Aktual). See [[supabase-migrations-manual]] for the 3 pending migration files.
44	- Auto-posting wired into `checkout_transaction` (sales → debit Kas/Bank + credit Pendapatan, plus debit HPP/credit Persediaan when the sale has recipe cost data) and `void_transaction` (posts a reversing entry). Expense recording (`finance/actions.ts` → `addExpense`) also auto-posts via the new `post_journal_entry` RPC — purchases hit Persediaan, other categories map to a fixed category→account table (`EXPENSE_CATEGORY_ACCOUNT` in that file).
45	- Payroll does NOT auto-post yet — payslip actions still write directly to tables with no RPC, deliberately deferred rather than expanding this delivery further. If asked to close this gap, same pattern as the expense hook applies.
46	- 5 new pages under `/business/<id>/accounting/`: `daftar-akun` (CRUD custom accounts, system accounts can't be deleted), `jurnal` (period-filtered list + manual multi-line entry form with live debit=credit balance check), `neraca` (balance sheet as-of a date, with an unclosed "Laba Berjalan" line in Modal since there's no formal period-closing process — if aset≠kewajiban+modal it flags a visible warning), `arus-kas` (cash flow from the Kas & Bank account only, bucketed into Operasional vs "Investasi & Pendanaan (manual)"), `anggaran` (monthly budget per pendapatan/beban account vs actual from the journal). All wired into a new "Akuntansi" sidebar group in `dashboard-shell.tsx` (hidden for `tiket` business type, same as the existing Keuangan/Laporan group).
47	- Verified pre-migration: all 5 pages render gracefully with empty/zero state (no crashes) since none of them gate on the new tables existing — only real financial correctness (auto-posting, balance changes) remains to verify once the migrations are applied.
48	- **Full E2E verification completed 2026-07-09** (see [[supabase-migrations-manual]] for details): expense auto-posting (Lain-lain → debit Beban Lain-lain/credit Kas & Bank, Neraca stays balanced) and the Anggaran/budgets UI (set target, Aktual pulled correctly from journal, variance/% computed correctly) both confirmed working. The whole accounting module (COA, Jurnal, Neraca, Arus Kas, Anggaran) is now fully exercised end-to-end, not just pre-migration render checks. Also seeded a superadmin panel (`/admin`) with Melan's first-ever real account — see [[project-purpose-saas-product]].

User wants KasirKu to grow toward a "mini ERP" (2026-07-08), modeled loosely on a reference prototype (`Koenang Resto` — a separate accounting + cost-control app, file at `D:\Users\ASTRI\Downloads\index.html`, an iframe shell only — actual module content in `modules/akuntansi.html`/`modules/costcontrol.html` was never shared). Explicit instruction: doesn't need to be complete, and must not disrupt the existing system — see [[project-purpose-saas-product]].

**Why:** the reference's sidebar reveals the target feature set even without the module internals: Akuntansi (COA/Jurnal/Neraca/Arus Kas/Target vs Aktual), Cost Control & HPP (kalkulator HPP, database bahan, cost control, laporan COGS, tren harga), Operasional (pembelian, stok, penjualan, invoice, kas harian, rekon rekening, supplier/hutang), SDM (absensi, payroll, lembur, THR, karyawan).

**Gap analysis against KasirKu's actual code (verified by reading source, not assumed):**
- Already covered, no rebuild needed: Laba Rugi (cash-basis, `reports/laba-rugi`), Payroll+Absensi, Kelola Produk/Bahan Baku, Riwayat Transaksi, Kelola Kasir.
- **Hitung HPP** — already exists: `products/[productId]/recipe/actions.ts` → `recalculateProductCost()` auto-recomputes `products.cost` from `product_recipes × ingredients.unit_cost` on every add/remove.
- **Cost Control (teori vs aktual)** — already exists in full inside `finance/page.tsx` (~line 187-256): COGS Teori (recipe-based) vs COGS Aktual (opening + pembelian − closing inventory), with a variance box and qualitative waste/efficiency notes. Not obvious from the nav alone — read the file before assuming this is missing.
- **Laporan COGS (per-produk/kategori breakdown)** — was genuinely missing; **built 2026-07-08** at `reports/cogs/page.tsx`, linked from the sidebar ("📐 Laporan COGS" in dashboard-shell.tsx) and cross-linked from `finance/page.tsx`'s Kontrol HPP section. Shows revenue/COGS/margin per category and per product, flags products with no HPP data (cost=0) and products under 20% margin.
- **Tren Harga bahan baku** — still missing, needs a new price-history table (`ingredients.unit_cost` only stores the current value, no history). Not started.
- Full double-entry **Akuntansi module** (COA, Jurnal, Neraca, Arus Kas, Target vs Aktual) — still entirely missing, and is a much bigger lift (new schema for accounts + journal lines, plus a decision on how it relates to the existing cash-basis Laba Rugi/Keuangan pages — replace or coexist?). Not started; user chose to do Cost Control/HPP first, accounting module "menyusul" (comes after).
- **Operasional gaps** not yet addressed: formal Pembelian (purchasing) records beyond the existing `expenses` category tagging, Supplier & Hutang (accounts payable) tracking — no supplier table exists yet.

**How to apply:** before building anything else from this reference, grep/read the relevant existing page first — this module has repeatedly turned out to already cover more than the sidebar-only feature list suggested. As of 2026-07-09 every item originally identified in this gap analysis has been built and verified E2E — no queued next candidate remains; ask the user what's next if resuming this thread.

**Formula audit — 2026-07-09**, after all the above was built, ran 4 parallel Explore agents auditing every calculation in the app (POS checkout/merchant-fee, HPP/COGS/weighted-avg cost, accounting/journal/balance-sheet, payroll/shift-close/ticket-pricing). Most formulas checked out clean (checkout math, weighted-average cost, Neraca arithmetic, Anggaran variance, payroll, shift-close, ticket pricing — the last one has existing passing unit tests, 38/38). **4 real bugs found, 1 fixed so far:**
1. **FIXED (commit bdbe337)**: Arus Kas (`accounting/arus-kas/page.tsx`) bucketed cash flow by `journal_entries.source`, but `public.post_journal_entry` (used by every purchase and expense posting, not just true manual entries) always writes `source='manual'` — so nearly all purchases/expenses were misclassified into "Investasi & Pendanaan" instead of "Operasional". Fixed by classifying by the counterparty account's type/code instead (modal→Pendanaan, Peralatan 1-500→Investasi, else→Operasional). Verified in browser: Beban Lain-lain, Bayar Utang Dagang, and a cash Persediaan purchase all correctly moved to "Aktivitas Operasional".
2. **FIXED (commit b928d51)**: `recalculateProductCost()` (`products/[productId]/recipe/actions.ts`) only used to re-fire on recipe line add/remove — never when an ingredient's `unit_cost` changed via `ingredients/actions.ts` `editIngredient`, `finance/actions.ts` `addExpense`, or `purchases/actions.ts` `addPurchase`, so `products.cost` (and downstream, `transaction_items.cost` snapshotted at sale time → COGS Teori) silently went stale. Fixed by extracting the calc into `src/lib/recalculate-product-cost.ts` (`recalculateProductCost` + a new `recalculateProductCostsForIngredient` that finds every product referencing a given ingredient and recalcs each) and calling the ingredient-scoped version from all three write sites whenever `unit_cost` actually changes. Verified in browser on "Toko Test Laporan": added Gula Pasir (50gr) to Roti Bakar's recipe (HPP → Rp1.350 at Rp27/gr), then edited Gula Pasir's price to Rp100/gr manually — Roti Bakar's HPP updated to Rp5.000 without touching the recipe. Then bought 100gr more via the Pembelian page (weighted avg → Rp106/gr) — HPP updated again to Rp5.300, confirming all three trigger paths work.
3. **FIXED (commit e02e62d, migration `20260709120000_fix_zero_total_hpp_posting.sql`)**: `checkout_transaction` only posted a journal entry `if v_total > 0`, but stock/ingredient consumption happens unconditionally — a 100%-discounted sale reduced inventory with no HPP/Persediaan journal line at all. Fixed by decoupling the Kas & Bank/Pendapatan lines (posted only when `v_total > 0`) from the HPP/Persediaan lines (posted independently whenever `v_total_cost > 0`), building `v_journal_lines` incrementally and only calling `private.post_journal` if at least 2 lines ended up in it. Mirrored the identical fix in `void_transaction`'s reversing entry. Verified end-to-end in browser on "Toko Test Laporan": sold 1 Roti Bakar (HPP Rp5.300) with a 100% order discount (INV-20260709-0001, total Rp0) — jurnal correctly posted a 2-line entry (debit 5-001 HPP / credit 1-200 Persediaan, Rp5.300, no Kas & Bank/Pendapatan lines). Then voided it with manager PIN — reversing entry correctly posted debit 1-200 / credit 5-001, Rp5.300. Neraca stayed balanced throughout.
4. **FIXED (commit 23c83ca)**: `purchases/actions.ts` and `finance/actions.ts` called the `post_journal_entry` RPC via `supabase.rpc(...)` without checking `{ error }`. Now `postExpenseJournal`/`postPurchaseJournal` return the error message (or null) instead of swallowing it, and both call sites plus the utang-payment RPC call in `addPurchasePayment` check it: on failure they log a `"warning"` activity entry (instead of the usual success level) with the error text, and return a form error telling the user the record saved but a manual correcting journal entry is needed at Akuntansi → Jurnal. Verified no regression on the happy path (a normal "Lain-lain" expense still saved silently with no error banner). The failure path itself wasn't exercised (would need deliberately breaking an account code) but the logic is a straightforward null-check/ternary, low risk.

**All 4 formula-audit bugs are now fixed** (commits bdbe337, b928d51, e02e62d, 23c83ca) — not yet pushed to origin as of the last fix. See [[supabase-migrations-manual]] if any future fix here needs a new migration.

**Supplier & Hutang (formal Pembelian) — built and verified E2E 2026-07-09**: migration `20260709110000_suppliers_purchases.sql` (see [[supabase-migrations-manual]]) adds `public.suppliers` (name/phone/address/notes, soft-delete), `public.purchases` (supplier_id nullable, category constrained to `'Bahan Baku'|'Barang Dagang'`, optional ingredient_id/product_id + qty, amount, paid_amount with a `paid_amount <= amount` check), and `public.purchase_payments` (installment log). Deliberately additive/separate from the existing `finance/actions.ts` `addExpense` "Pembelian Bahan Baku/Barang Dagang" categories — this is a new, more structured flow for supplier-attributed purchases that can be paid partially or fully on credit, not a replacement.
- New pages: `suppliers/page.tsx` (CRUD list + outstanding-utang badge computed from purchases) and `purchases/page.tsx` (record a purchase — mirrors `add-expense-form.tsx`'s ingredient/product conditional UI and weighted-average cost recalc exactly, plus a 3-way payment-mode picker: Lunas Sekarang / Bayar Sebagian / Semua Utang — with inline "+ Bayar" installment forms per unpaid purchase row).
- `purchases/actions.ts` `addPurchase` posts a journal entry via the same `post_journal_entry` RPC pattern as `finance/actions.ts` (debit 1-200 Persediaan for the full amount; credit 1-001 Kas & Bank for whatever's paid now, credit 2-001 Utang Dagang for the remainder — 2 or 3 lines depending on payment mode). `addPurchasePayment` posts debit 2-001 / credit 1-001 for each installment and rejects overpayment past the remaining balance. Ingredient purchases also insert into `ingredient_price_history` (source `'pembelian'`) same as the expense flow, see [[mini-erp-scope]]'s Tren Harga section above.
- Nav: "🧾 Pembelian & Hutang" and "🏬 Supplier" added to the Operasional sidebar group (not fnb-gated — retail businesses get both too, just without the ingredient option; tiket excluded like the rest of Operasional's inventory items).
- Verified in browser: added supplier "CV Sumber Rejeki", bought 500gr Gula Pasir for Rp15.000 fully on credit → journal posted debit Persediaan/credit Utang Dagang Rp15.000 correctly (2-line entry, no Kas & Bank line since paid_amount=0), stock updated 1000→1500gr. Paid Rp10.000 installment → journal posted debit Utang Dagang/credit Kas & Bank Rp10.000, purchase row updated to "Sisa Rp5.000", supplier badge showed "Utang Rp5.000", Neraca stayed balanced throughout (Aset = Kewajiban + Modal confirmed after each step).
- UI quirk hit during testing, useful for future preview-tool sessions on this project: clicking a `useActionState`-wired submit button (`<form action={formAction}>`, a React-specific mechanism) immediately after `window.location.href` navigation can silently no-op if it fires before hydration completes — no network request, no error, just nothing happens. Re-clicking (or waiting a beat) after confirming the click actually landed fixes it. This is distinct from the earlier-documented plain-`onClick`-button pattern (edit-ingredient-form.tsx-style inline forms), which doesn't have this hydration race since... actually both need hydration; the symptom just presents differently (edit forms fail to open at all if unhydrated, vs. server-action forms open fine but silently eat the submit).

**Tren Harga bahan baku — built and verified E2E 2026-07-09**: new `public.ingredient_price_history` table (migration `20260709100000_ingredient_price_history.sql`, see [[supabase-migrations-manual]]) is an append-only log (`business_id`, `ingredient_id`, `unit_cost`, `source` in `awal`/`pembelian`/`manual`, `created_at`), backfilled with each existing ingredient's current price as an `awal` row. Two write sites: `finance/actions.ts` `addExpense` inserts a `pembelian` row when a "Pembelian Bahan Baku" expense changes the weighted-average `unit_cost`; `ingredients/actions.ts` `editIngredient` inserts a `manual` row when the manual-edit form changes `unit_cost` (compares against the pre-update value fetched first). New page `reports/price-trend/page.tsx` — period filter (30/90 hari/semua), naik/turun-harga summary counts, and a `<details>`-per-ingredient list (server-component-friendly, no client JS) showing current vs baseline price and full history on expand. Nav link "🏷️ Tren Harga" added next to "Bahan Baku" in the Operasional sidebar group (fnb-only, same gate as Bahan Baku itself). Verified in browser: bought Gula Pasir at a higher price → showed up as `pembelian` entry and flagged "Naik Harga: 1 bahan"; edited its price manually via the ingredients page's inline edit (a client-state form with no `<form>` tag — Simpan is a plain button, so driving it via preview tools requires the native-setter + dispatchEvent('input') trick, not `preview_fill`, to get React's onChange to fire) → showed up as a third `manual` entry, history list correctly ordered newest-first (Edit manual Rp25 → Pembelian Rp21 → Awal Rp18).

**Akuntansi module — built 2026-07-08** (user explicitly chose auto-posting from transactions, and all 4 reports at once, overriding the "doesn't need to be complete" framing for this specific piece):
- Schema: `public.accounts` (Chart of Accounts, seeded per-business via trigger + backfill with a standard Indonesian F&B/retail COA — Kas & Bank, Persediaan, Utang Dagang, Modal Pemilik, Pendapatan Penjualan, Beban Pokok Penjualan, Beban Gaji/Sewa/Listrik/Marketing/Perlengkapan/Lain-lain), `public.journal_entries` + `public.journal_lines` (double-entry, journal tables are SELECT-only from the client — all writes go through `private.post_journal()` so an unbalanced entry can never be persisted), `public.budgets` (Target vs Aktual). See [[supabase-migrations-manual]] for the 3 pending migration files.
- Auto-posting wired into `checkout_transaction` (sales → debit Kas/Bank + credit Pendapatan, plus debit HPP/credit Persediaan when the sale has recipe cost data) and `void_transaction` (posts a reversing entry). Expense recording (`finance/actions.ts` → `addExpense`) also auto-posts via the new `post_journal_entry` RPC — purchases hit Persediaan, other categories map to a fixed category→account table (`EXPENSE_CATEGORY_ACCOUNT` in that file).
- Payroll does NOT auto-post yet — payslip actions still write directly to tables with no RPC, deliberately deferred rather than expanding this delivery further. If asked to close this gap, same pattern as the expense hook applies.
- 5 new pages under `/business/<id>/accounting/`: `daftar-akun` (CRUD custom accounts, system accounts can't be deleted), `jurnal` (period-filtered list + manual multi-line entry form with live debit=credit balance check), `neraca` (balance sheet as-of a date, with an unclosed "Laba Berjalan" line in Modal since there's no formal period-closing process — if aset≠kewajiban+modal it flags a visible warning), `arus-kas` (cash flow from the Kas & Bank account only, bucketed into Operasional vs "Investasi & Pendanaan (manual)"), `anggaran` (monthly budget per pendapatan/beban account vs actual from the journal). All wired into a new "Akuntansi" sidebar group in `dashboard-shell.tsx` (hidden for `tiket` business type, same as the existing Keuangan/Laporan group).
- Verified pre-migration: all 5 pages render gracefully with empty/zero state (no crashes) since none of them gate on the new tables existing — only real financial correctness (auto-posting, balance changes) remains to verify once the migrations are applied.
- **Full E2E verification completed 2026-07-09** (see [[supabase-migrations-manual]] for details): expense auto-posting (Lain-lain → debit Beban Lain-lain/credit Kas & Bank, Neraca stays balanced) and the Anggaran/budgets UI (set target, Aktual pulled correctly from journal, variance/% computed correctly) both confirmed working. The whole accounting module (COA, Jurnal, Neraca, Arus Kas, Anggaran) is now fully exercised end-to-end, not just pre-migration render checks. Also seeded a superadmin panel (`/admin`) with Melan's first-ever real account — see [[project-purpose-saas-product]].

## 1. Payroll action files

**`src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/payroll/actions.ts`** — no journal posting exists here at all today. Key facts:

- `createPayslip(businessId, cashierId, periodStart, periodEnd)` (lines 11-82): computes `basePay = dailyRate * hadir_count` from attendance, then inserts into `payslips` (only base pay, no adjustments yet). This is a **creation** step, not a "paid" step — there is no concept of marking a payslip as "paid" anywhere in the schema/code (no `paid_at`, `status`, or payment-method column on `payslips`).
- `addPayslipAdjustment(businessId, payslipId, type, label, amount)` (lines 92-142): inserts into `payslip_adjustments` (`type` is `"tunjangan"` allowance or `"potongan"` deduction). This is what THR/lembur/bonuses currently flow through — there's no dedicated THR/lembur field, just generic tunjangan/potongan labels typed in free text via `create-payslip-form.tsx` / `add-adjustment-form.tsx`.
- `deletePayslip`, `deletePayslipAdjustment` — plain deletes, revalidate only.

None of these call `post_journal_entry`. The "total diterima" (what actually gets paid out) is computed client-side in `payroll/[payslipId]/page.tsx:60`: `basePay + totalTunjangan - totalPotongan` — this final number only exists at render time in the detail page, not stored anywhere. So there is no single action today that represents "money left the till/bank for payroll" — you'll need to decide whether to post the journal at `createPayslip` time (using base_pay only) or add a new "finalize/pay" action that also includes adjustment totals (recommended, so THR/lembur/potongan affect the journal amount too).

Payroll DB schema (`supabase/migrations/20260706100000_payroll.sql`):
- `payslips`: `business_id, cashier_id, period_start, period_end, daily_rate, hadir_count, izin_count, sakit_count, alpa_count, base_pay, created_at` — **no payment-method / paid-status column**.
- `payslip_adjustments`: `payslip_id, type ('tunjangan'|'potongan'), label, amount`.

## 2. Existing auto-posting pattern

**`src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/finance/actions.ts`**

```ts
const EXPENSE_CATEGORY_ACCOUNT: Record<string, string> = {
  Sewa: "5-102",
  "Gaji & Upah": "5-100",
  "Listrik & Air": "5-101",
  Marketing: "5-103",
  Perlengkapan: "5-104",
  "Lain-lain": "5-999",
};

async function postExpenseJournal(
  supabase, businessId, date, category, amount, isPurchase,
): Promise<string | null> {
  const debitAccount = isPurchase ? "1-200" : EXPENSE_CATEGORY_ACCOUNT[category] ?? "5-999";
  const { error } = await supabase.rpc("post_journal_entry", {
    p_business_id: businessId,
    p_date: date,
    p_description: `Pengeluaran: ${category}`,
    p_lines: [
      { account_code: debitAccount, debit: amount, credit: 0 },
      { account_code: "1-001", debit: 0, credit: amount },
    ],
  });
  return error?.message ?? null;
}
```

Note "Gaji & Upah" already maps to `5-100` (Beban Gaji) — this is the manual-expense path, separate from payroll module.

Called from `addExpense` (lines 177-201): `journalError` captured, then used to (a) mark the `logActivity` severity `"warning"` vs `"info"`, and (b) surface a user-facing message: `"...tapi gagal posting ke jurnal (${journalError}). Tambahkan jurnal koreksi manual di halaman Akuntansi → Jurnal."` — the DB row is never rolled back, failures are just surfaced, not swallowed (per commit `23c83ca`, which changed `postExpenseJournal`/`postPurchaseJournal` from fire-and-forget `await supabase.rpc(...)` to capturing `{ error }` and threading it through).

**`src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/purchases/actions.ts`**

```ts
async function postPurchaseJournal(
  supabase, businessId, date, description, amount, paidAmount,
): Promise<string | null> {
  const lines = [{ account_code: "1-200", debit: amount, credit: 0 }];
  if (paidAmount > 0) lines.push({ account_code: "1-001", debit: 0, credit: paidAmount });
  const sisaUtang = amount - paidAmount;
  if (sisaUtang > 0) lines.push({ account_code: "2-001", debit: 0, credit: sisaUtang });
  const { error } = await supabase.rpc("post_journal_entry", {
    p_business_id: businessId, p_date: date, p_description: description, p_lines: lines,
  });
  return error?.message ?? null;
}
```

Same pattern: called from `addPurchase` (lines 174-200), and a third inline call in `addPurchasePayment` (lines 265-293) for paying down utang (debits `2-001`, credits `1-001`). All three follow the identical shape: insert business row → call rpc → capture `error?.message` → log activity with `"warning"` severity + message if failed → return a friendly `error` string telling the user to add a manual correcting entry, without undoing the saved record.

## 3. `post_journal_entry` RPC / `private.post_journal`

`supabase/migrations/20260708300000_accounting_core.sql`:

- `public.post_journal_entry(p_business_id uuid, p_date timestamptz, p_description text, p_lines jsonb)` (line 205) — security-definer RPC, checks `private.owns_business(p_business_id)`, requires non-empty `p_description`, then calls `private.post_journal(p_business_id, coalesce(p_date, now()), p_description, 'manual', null, p_lines)`. Only the four params above are exposed to the client RPC (source is hardcoded `'manual'`, source_id `null` — this is the one used by finance/purchases). Granted to `authenticated`.
- `private.post_journal(p_business_id, p_date, p_description, p_source, p_source_id, p_lines jsonb)` (line 142) — the real mechanical helper, used directly (via `perform`) from other security-definer contexts (checkout/void RPCs) when they need a specific `source`/`source_id` (e.g. `'penjualan'`, `'void'`, `'pembelian'`, `'beban'`, `'payroll'` — see `journal_entries.source` check constraint, line 33-35, which **already includes `'payroll'` as a valid source value**, anticipating this feature).
  - Validates `p_lines` has ≥2 entries.
  - Sums debit/credit across lines; raises `unbalanced journal entry: debit % <> credit %` if they don't match (rounded to 2dp).
  - Inserts one row into `journal_entries`, then one row into `journal_lines` per line, resolving `account_code` → `account_id` via `accounts` table scoped to `business_id`; raises `account not found: %` if a code doesn't exist for that business.
  - Returns the new `journal_entries.id`.

Since `post_journal_entry` (the public RPC) hardcodes `source: 'manual'`, if you want the payroll journal entries tagged with `source = 'payroll'` (which the schema already supports) you'd need either a new dedicated RPC (e.g. `public.post_payroll_journal_entry` calling `private.post_journal(..., 'payroll', p_payslip_id, p_lines)`) or just reuse `post_journal_entry` and accept `source = 'manual'` like expenses/purchases currently do (they also just use the generic RPC, not their own `source` tags, despite `'beban'`/`'pembelian'` being valid enum values too — so the existing pattern doesn't bother with per-module `source`).

## 4. Chart of Accounts (COA) seed

`private.seed_default_accounts` in `supabase/migrations/20260708300000_accounting_core.sql` (lines 90-108), seeded per business on `businesses` insert trigger:

| code | name | type | normal_balance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1-001 | Kas & Bank | aset | debit |
| 1-100 | Piutang Usaha | aset | debit |
| 1-200 | Persediaan | aset | debit |
| 1-500 | Peralatan | aset | debit |
| 2-001 | Utang Dagang | kewajiban | kredit |
| **2-100** | **Utang Gaji** | kewajiban | kredit |
| 3-001 | Modal Pemilik | modal | kredit |
| 3-100 | Laba Ditahan | modal | kredit |
| 4-001 | Pendapatan Penjualan | pendapatan | kredit |
| 5-001 | Beban Pokok Penjualan (HPP) | beban | debit |
| **5-100** | **Beban Gaji** | beban | debit |
| 5-101 | Beban Listrik & Air | beban | debit |
| 5-102 | Beban Sewa | beban | debit |
| 5-103 | Beban Marketing | beban | debit |
| 5-104 | Beban Perlengkapan | beban | debit |
| 5-999 | Beban Lain-lain | beban | debit |

There is only **one** cash/bank account: `1-001 Kas & Bank`. There is no separate "Bank" account and no "Kas Harian" account in the seed — everything liquid is lumped into `1-001`.

For payroll you already have both a P&L side (`5-100 Beban Gaji`) and a liability side (`2-100 Utang Gaji`, unused by any code today) available — useful if you want to support "accrue now, pay later" (debit 5-100 / credit 2-100) followed by a separate payment posting (debit 2-100 / credit 1-001), mirroring the purchases→utang-dagang pattern. Simpler: straight cash-basis (debit 5-100 / credit 1-001) at payslip-paid time, same shape as `postExpenseJournal`.

## 5. THR/lembur/kas vs bank in payroll

None exists. Confirmed via grep across the whole `payroll` directory for `thr|lembur|overtime|bonus|kas harian|payment_method|paid_via|pay_from|bank` — zero matches. The only mechanism for extra pay/deductions is the generic `payslip_adjustments` table (`type: 'tunjangan' | 'potongan'`, freeform `label`/`amount`) — so a THR or lembur bonus today is just entered as a `tunjangan` row with a custom label, not a first-class concept. There is also no payment-method selector anywhere in payroll UI (`create-payslip-form.tsx`, `add-adjustment-form.tsx`) — no Kas-vs-Bank choice; everything would map to the single `1-001 Kas & Bank` account, consistent with expenses/purchases which also always credit `1-001` regardless of method.

## 6. `EXPENSE_CATEGORY_ACCOUNT` shape

```ts

  Sewa: "5-102",
  "Gaji & Upah": "5-100",
  "Listrik & Air": "5-101",
  Marketing: "5-103",
  Perlengkapan: "5-104",
  "Lain-lain": "5-999",
};
```
`finance/actions.ts:16-23` — a flat `string -> account_code` map keyed by the exact category label shown in the expense form dropdown, with `EXPENSE_CATEGORY_ACCOUNT[category] ?? "5-999"` as a defensive fallback to "Beban Lain-lain" (comment above it explains categories outside the dropdown shouldn't occur since the form restricts choices). For payroll you likely don't need a map at all since there's only one expense category (gaji) — just hardcode debit `5-100` (or `2-100` if accruing) the way `isPurchase` hardcodes `1-200` in the same function.

## Implementation notes for your hookup

1. Decide the trigger point: `createPayslip` (base pay only, before adjustments exist) vs a new explicit "finalize/pay" action that sums `base_pay + tunjangan - potongan` from `payslip_adjustments` (mirrors the `totalDiterima` calc in `payroll/[payslipId]/page.tsx:57-60`). Given tunjangan/potongan can be added after creation, a dedicated "mark as paid" action (new, doesn't exist yet) that locks in the final total and posts the journal in one shot is the closest analogue to `addExpense`/`addPurchase` — otherwise THR/lembur added later won't be reflected in any journal entry.
2. Follow the exact `postExpenseJournal`/`postPurchaseJournal` shape: a private helper returning `Promise<string | null>`, called after the DB write, feeding into `journalError` for both `logActivity` severity/message and the returned `{ error }` state, without rolling back the payroll row on failure.
3. Suggested lines: `{ account_code: "5-100", debit: total, credit: 0 }, { account_code: "1-001", debit: 0, credit: total }` (cash-basis, matches expense pattern) — or the two-step accrual variant using `2-100 Utang Gaji` if you want a "pay later" flow like purchases/utang-dagang.</result>

For browser-preview verification of KasirKu (created 2026-07-03): test login `claude.test.reports@gmail.com` / `test-kasirku-123` (email confirmation is disabled on the Supabase project, signup returns a session immediately). Business "Toko Test Laporan" (F&B, id `7c483432-1c9a-4f03-a0b2-aa4d89f7f5e9`) with cashier "Melan" PIN `1234`, manager "Manajer Test" PIN `9999` (for void authorization), PPN 10% + service 5% enabled (affects checkout totals), products Kopi Susu/Roti Bakar, an open shift, 2 transactions on 2026-07-03, and table "Meja 1" (qr_slug `CWsFCMmosD7O`, id `8b67c355-65a2-47d3-a79a-a935ede87dd3`) for self-order testing. Self-orders can be seeded directly via REST insert into `self_orders` + `self_order_items` using the owner access token from the browser cookie (`sb-…-auth-token`, base64 JSON) since the customer-facing RPC is still missing on remote (see [[supabase-migrations-manual]]). Safe to reuse or delete — it's a separate auth user, invisible to the real owner account.

Same owner account also has a ticket-venue business "Kolam Renang Test" (id `f43c8529-7fe5-4074-9e98-43335da31267`, 🎟️ Tempat Wisata/Tiket) with cashier "Kasir Tiket" (role manajer) — PIN reset to `1234` on 2026-07-07 via Kelola Kasir (original PIN unknown), an open shift, ticket categories Pengunjung/Rp25.000/Penunggu/Rp10.000/Yoga clas/Rp340.000, and members "Budi Member" (M-0001) plus test-added "Budi Tester" (MBR-001, member_price Rp0 for Pengunjung). Confirmed working end-to-end: manual physical ticket numbers on checkout (duplicate number correctly rejected with a friendly error), member lookup/pricing in POS, ticket-reports reconciliation list, CSV export (`/ticket-reports/export?type=transactions&period=today`), member barcode card (`/members/<id>/card`, uses jsbarcode), and transaction detail/void page.

**Why:** the real owner's password is unknown, and the proxy redirects all /business routes to /login, so preview verification needs its own account.

**How to apply:** log in at /login with these credentials, then navigate to /business/<id>/... pages. Note: Turbopack on the slow G: drive sometimes serves stale CSS after globals.css edits — `rm -rf .next` and restart the dev server if new Tailwind utilities don't apply. See [[supabase-migrations-manual]]. The POS PIN keypad (pin-screen.tsx) is plain React state, not a real input — driving it with `preview_eval` by firing all 4 digit clicks in one synchronous block silently fails (React batches the clicks and reads a stale `pin` closure each time, so it never reaches length 4 and neither succeeds nor shows an error). Use separate `preview_click` calls per digit (e.g. `.grid.grid-cols-3.gap-3 button:nth-child(n)`), one per tool call, so each click gets its own render cycle.
